Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual ARC

1. Treat only the active instance's test and demos as task state. 2. Parse exact dimensions and compare input/output geometry before proposing a rule. For expanded outputs, segment by the factor ratios (e.g. output height/input height and width/input width), then compare candidate tiles or blocks against the input, including rotation/reflection and axis reversal. Check the proposed mapping cell-by-cell against every demo; do not infer simple scaling or mirroring from output size or resemblance alone. For sparse recoloring tasks, record the complete changed-cell mask (both recolored and unchanged candidates) and test a concrete rule against every marked and unmarked cell; visual alignment or apparent gaps alone is not validation.

If demos show rotated or reflected copies, enumerate the unique dihedral orientations (four rotations and their reflections) before searching. Match all target placements against the original input, collect and deduplicate their cells, then apply changes; do not let earlier edits create new matches. Check that this procedure reproduces every demo's changed-cell mask before using it on the test.
4. Before requesting a demo, state internally the specific unresolved rule choice it would distinguish, and compare the expected information against its one-point cost. First re-derive candidate rules from all existing examples, including unchanged objects and regions—not merely visible edits. Request only when a plausible pair of alternatives predicts different outcomes on the next example; otherwise do not spend a demo on an open-ended hope for clarity. After incorrect feedback, never repeat the same prediction unchanged. Compare predicted edits cell-by-cell with the test and recheck the full changed-cell mask against every demo. Identify the falsified assumption before choosing a correction. Request a genuinely discriminating demo only if plausible alternatives remain unresolved; never submit a guessed variation.
5. Apply only validated edits to a copy of the test. Verify dimensions, every row width, values, and changed coordinates against the demos. The final line must contain exactly one action JSON object; finish only after the instance is over.
